messages:
alex: quick question — we saw a tenant in eu-west hit CB and then requests fell back to the cheaper global lane, but the tenant had a header override `X-Tenant-Route: prefer-affinity`. Should we let that header trump fallback when capacity is low?

maria: hmm, the intent was header-affinity > region-fallback, but iirc there's an intermediate step where circuit-breaker backoff flips a soft flag that forces cross-region.

jamie: correct. current pipeline: match route -> check quotas -> check CB -> compute fallback lane. CB sets `degraded=true` and that triggers region failover regardless of header.

dinesh: that explains telemetry spikes. our dashboard shows "fallback_count" rising with `degraded=true` but no per-tenant override metric. we should add a new trace tag so we can filter by header overrides.

olivia: from Console UX POV, we need to surface per-route header overrides + CB state in the rollout view. operators currently only see final lane decision, not the precedence chain.

alex: proposal: change precedence so header-affinity is evaluated after CB but with a guard: if CB is open and error-rate > 10% then header-affinity applies only for sticky sessions (same conn), otherwise ignore. Means we preserve safety but allow affinity when safe.

maria: that feels complicated. i'd prefer a simpler policy: add a tenant-level flag `allow-header-override-during-degrade` (default false). If enabled, header-affinity can win even when CB tripped. Simpler to reason about and explicit.

jamie: implementation notes — router currently applies rules in this order: route.match -> header.normalization -> quota.check -> cb.evaluate -> lane.select. To support maria's flag we could: after cb.evaluate, if cb.tripped && tenantFlag true then re-evaluate header.normalization and lane.select with header priority. Minimal changes.

Code sketch jamie pasted:
```yaml
router:
  - match: route
  - normalize_headers:
      preserve: [X-Tenant-Route]
  - quota_check
  - circuit_breaker: evaluate
  - post_cb_reconcile:
      if: tenant.allow_header_override_during_degrade
      then: reapply_header_affinity
```

alex: also need telemetry: increment `override_applied` tag when reapply_header_affinity flips lane. add histogram of token-latency per lane so we can see cost impact.

dinesh: i'll add a grafana panel and an alert: `fallback_rate > 5% AND override_applied > 0` -> PM sync. want to see which tenants are enabling the flag.

maria: security ask: ensure header normalization prevents header spoofing. only accept X-Tenant-Route when it matches signed header or internal proxy. we already have HMAC header signing but not wired into router check.

jamie: good catch — add `header_signature` check into normalize_headers step. snippet:
```
if X-Tenant-Route and not verify_signature(X-Tenant-Sig): drop X-Tenant-Route
```

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for router:v2-reconcile (5% traffic). logs at https://deploys.internal/redwood/router/v2

olivia: for Console change, i'll add a stack in the rollout panel: Decision chain -> [route match] -> [quota] -> [cb state] -> [header override check] -> [final lane]. show small icon if tenant.flag=true.

alex: action items: jamie to PR minimal router change + header sig check, dinesh to add telemetry panel & alert, olivia to prototype console UX, maria to draft policy text for tenant flag and default. i'll run a comms thread to sign off on safety.

maria: +1, thanks.

jamie: will open PR today, link here when done.

deploy-bot: canary progressing: 0 errors after 30m, 5% -> 20%

alex: closing loop — if PR lands and canary looks good we flip default=false but enable opt-in for a couple of test tenants. we'll re-evaluate after 48h. :thumbsup:
